sources.model: Copernicus Marine GLORYS12V1 global ocean physics reanalysis (GLOBAL_MULTIYEAR_PHY_001_030), daily means centred on each analysis time, read from the native 1/12 deg NetCDF-4 files; each 0.5 deg cell the mean of the native points inside it, levels interpolated linearly to the app depths.
sources.argo: Argo GDAC via erddap.ifremer.fr (ArgoFloats); adjusted values for delayed-mode and adjusted profiles, data-centre QC flags 1, 2, 5, 8 kept, then the global-range, regional-range, spike and stuck-value tests re-run; the closest profile to each analysis within 1.5 days
sources.bgc: BGC-Argo synthetic profiles via erddap.ifremer.fr (ArgoFloats-synthetic-BGC): chlorophyll-a (mg/m3) and dissolved oxygen (umol/kg), adjusted values only (delayed-mode or adjusted; raw real-time values are not used), QC flags 1, 2, 5, 8 and range checks. The model has no biogeochemistry: chlorophyll and oxygen come from the floats only.
sources.bathymetry: ETOPO1 via upwell.pfeg.noaa.gov ERDDAP (etopo180), sampled every 0.1 deg
sources.track: IBTrACS v04r01 North Indian basin (NOAA NCEI); JTWC 1-minute and IMD 3-minute winds

citations.text: Generated using E.U. Copernicus Marine Service Information: Global Ocean Physics Reanalysis (GLOBAL_MULTIYEAR_PHY_001_030, GLORYS12V1, daily means), doi:10.48670/moi-00021. Lellouche, J.-M. et al. (2021), The Copernicus Global 1/12° Oceanic and Sea Ice GLORYS12 Reanalysis, Front. Earth Sci. 9:698876, doi:10.3389/feart.2021.698876. Used under the Copernicus Marine Service commitments and licence (marine.copernicus.eu/user-corner/service-commitments-and-licence).

These data were collected and made freely available by the International Argo Program and the national programs that contribute to it (https://argo.ucsd.edu, https://www.ocean-ops.org). The Argo Program is part of the Global Ocean Observing System. Argo (2000), Argo float data and metadata from Global Data Assembly Centre (Argo GDAC), SEANOE, doi:10.17882/42182; accessed through the Ifremer ERDDAP server.

Chlorophyll-a and dissolved oxygen from BGC-Argo synthetic profiles (Argo GDAC, doi:10.17882/42182). Bittig, H. C. et al. (2019), A BGC-Argo guide: planning, deployment, data handling and usage, Front. Mar. Sci. 6:502, doi:10.3389/fmars.2019.00502.

Amante, C. and B. W. Eakins (2009), ETOPO1 1 Arc-Minute Global Relief Model: Procedures, Data Sources and Analysis, NOAA Technical Memorandum NESDIS NGDC-24, doi:10.7289/V5C8276M. (ETOPO1 is superseded by ETOPO 2022.)

Knapp, K. R., M. C. Kruk, D. H. Levinson, H. J. Diamond and C. J. Neumann (2010), The International Best Track Archive for Climate Stewardship (IBTrACS), Bull. Amer. Meteor. Soc. 91, 363–376, doi:10.1175/2009BAMS2755.1; IBTrACS v04r01, NOAA NCEI, doi:10.25921/82ty-9e16. Positions and winds from RSMC New Delhi (IMD) and the Joint Typhoon Warning Center.

model.read: NetCDF-4 (HDF5) chunks in HTTPS byte ranges by data-pipeline/nc4.py

checked_against.levels: the first and the first at or below 1000 m
checked_against.result: identical int16 values in the map box

attrs.title: daily mean fields from Global Ocean Physics Analysis and Forecast updated Daily

model.filled_cells: model values in cells without model water are filled from neighbours; mask.wet marks the cells that hold model water

qc.values: CHLA_ADJUSTED and DOXY_ADJUSTED only; raw CHLA and DOXY are never used
qc.pressure: PRES_ADJUSTED where present, else PRES; flag 1, 2, 5 or 8
qc.matched_to: the selected core Argo profile with the same float and cycle
qc.levels: gridded onto argo.levels like temperature; gaps wider than 20/40/80 m stay gaps
